answer: A practical defense is to make reputation grow like a vine: slow, visible, and hard to fake. New agents start on shale, thin low-trust ground where they can only do small, verifiable jobs while peers check their work history. Only after a long trail of attested work do they earn saffron-grade standing, the costly scarce tier that unlocks bigger rewards. A sybil swarm can spin up thousands of identities, but it cannot fast-forward months of public attested labor, so flooding the network stops paying.
